PullRequest.Title: Agents - Fix pill height for top-row pickers in new session background
PullRequest.Body:
This pull request addresses the inconsistency in pill heights for the top-row branch/worktree pickers when the new session page has a background. The following changes were made:

- Updated the CSS in `chatWidget.css` to ensure that the top-row pickers maintain a height of **24px**, aligning them with the rest of the pill controls, while keeping the bottom toolbar at **22px**.
- Added computed-style regression tests in `chatView.test.ts` to validate the height of both picker surfaces.

These changes ensure a consistent user interface across different components of the session page. Note that validation of the changes is pending due to incomplete dependencies.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or reveal the experimental new-session composer with a chat background, including repository and workspace picker pills
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing widget construction creates one repository toolbar, then browser style calculation and layout must complete before the composer is painted. The diff adds one fixed-height declaration to that existing style pass; no new JavaScript geometry read or forced synchronous relayout is introduced.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One matching repository action-bar element per visible new-session composer. Repository action count remains children of that one bar and does not increase the number of selector matches or boundary calls.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single renderer/UI-thread style and layout pass for the visible composer; no queue, limiter, asynchronous fan-out, or concurrent boundary work is added by the diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No application cache is read or invalidated. Cold stylesheet parsing gains one small rule; subsequent style recalculation uses the browser's normal stylesheet state. There is no changed positive, negative, or coalescing behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed production hunk is a static CSS height declaration, and the traced DOM creation establishes one matching toolbar container without any changed boundary or repeated callback.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact style-selector matching cost is not measured, but cardinality is bounded to one relevant action bar and the declaration performs no script-driven layout read, so no realistic user-visible regression mechanism is present.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The rule changes geometry from the inherited 22px control height to 24px during an already-required layout pass; it does not add repeated layout, rendering fan-out, or expensive boundary work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Run the chat-view computed-style regression test
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The test already obtains computed-style objects for both picker surfaces; the diff reads each object's height property and compares two additional strings. This is test-only and does not affect product startup or rendering.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Two constant property reads and two constant expected values per single test execution; cost does not scale with sessions, repositories, messages, or user input.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The test remains synchronous and serial; no added workers, subprocesses, IPC, filesystem, database, or network calls are introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache behavior changes. The existing browser test DOM and computed-style snapshots are reused.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed lines only access `.height` on already-created CSSStyleDeclaration objects and extend the assertion literals.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material; added work is constant and confined to tests.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. Constant test-only property accesses do not create a product performance regression or meaningful test throughput degradation.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over the full two-file diff. Checked rendering/layout sensitivity, selector cardinality, test-only computed-style access, lifecycle, concurrency, caching, and transitive expensive boundaries. No reportable performance issue or qualifying shipped-regression fix was found.
